name: PushOwl
summary: Shopify web-push and omnichannel marketing, now part of Brevo. One-click push lets stores re-engage shoppers who never leave an email, recovering abandoned carts and browsing sessions, then add email, SMS and WhatsApp on Brevo's deliverability stack. Usage-based pricing: you pay for what you send, not list size.
best_for: Shopify stores that want to win back abandoned carts and browsing sessions with one-click web push, reaching shoppers who never handed over an email, and then layer in email and SMS, starting on a free tier that does something
skip_if: you're not on Shopify (it's built exclusively for it), or you need a full standalone email platform: the 500-email bundle cap means heavy senders keep paying extra per credit
honest_knock: The bundles are push-first: every paid tier still caps included email low (1,000 a month on Plus and 1,500 on Power in the app on 17 November 2026, against 500 on the free bundle), so 'omnichannel' email at any real volume means buying separate credits, and consumption-based pricing gets harder to predict as your sends climb. It's also Shopify-exclusive, so it becomes a dead end the day you move platforms.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month ($180/yr) for 10,000 web push messages

plans.name: Basic
plans.includes: 500 emails and 500 web push notifications a month, no SMS credits

plans.name: Plus
plans.includes: 10,000 web push (10,000-30,000 band), 1,000 emails in the app, abandoned-cart automation

plans.name: Power
plans.includes: 25,000 up to unlimited web push, 1,500 emails in the app, flash-sale and browse-abandonment triggers, segmentation

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/pushowl and in our own test that day; earlier: prices read 2026-08-17 in a browser and re-read unchanged on 2026-10-04 on pushowl.com/pricing, with both billing toggles) This is priced per channel and then added up, which is the part worth understanding before you compare it with anything. Each bundle sets a separate rate for email, web push and SMS, and the monthly figure is their sum. Basic is $0 and covers 500 emails and 500 web push notifications a month with no SMS credits. Plus is $19/month for 10,000 web push (10,000-30,000 band) and adds abandoned-cart automation. Power is $79/month for 25,000 up to unlimited web push, with flash-sale and browse-abandonment triggers, segmentation and custom attribution windows. Yearly billing is advertised at 10% off, and 20% on the web push side of Plus: billed yearly, Plus shows $15 a month and Power $71, with email at 500 sends on Basic and SMS at zero credits in every bundle as read on 4 October 2026 (on 17 November 2026 the app showed 1,000 emails on Plus and 1,500 on Power). It is Shopify-only. Read again on 17 November 2026: the Shopify listing, now titled Brevo PushOwl: Email, Push, SMS with Brevo PushOwl as the developer, shows the Basic Bundle free (500 web push notifications a month, emails from 500, unlimited subscribers), the Plus Bundle at $19 a month or $180 a year ($15 a month) and the Power Bundle at $79 a month or $852 a year ($71 a month), at 4.8 from 2,322 reviews. The Plus card now gives emails from 1,000 a month. In our own test the same day on a Shopify development store the dashboard pricing page showed the Basic Bundle as the current plan at $0.00 with 0 of 500 web push impressions and 0 of 500 email credits used, Plus at $19.00 with 10,000 push and 1,000 emails, Power at $79.00 with 25,000 push and 1,500 emails, and no SMS credits on any plan, with a Buy credits button. Abandoned cart recovery was marked as available on the Plus bundle and browse abandonment on the Power bundle. Selecting Plus opened Shopify's approval screen: $19.00 every 30 days, with an Add payment method row and no line saying the charge would not be billed, so we did not approve it.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested PushOwl (Brevo PushOwl: Email,Push,SMS in the listing) on a Shopify development store: the install, the dashboard that opens through Shopify without a Brevo account, the Welcome notifications flow that was already on with a preview, a Rival Spin to win popup preview that was not saved, the free Basic plan with 500 pushes and 500 e-mails a month, the locked Abandoned cart recovery, Browse abandonment and Shipping notifications, the Plus approval screen (not approved) and the uninstall dialog, which asks for a reason. Nothing was sent, paid or saved. Install: the listing apps.shopify.com/pushowl is now called Brevo PushOwl: Email,Push,SMS (developer Brevo PushOwl), with the label Free plan available and a rating of 4.8 from 2,321 reviews on the listing today (2,322 in our test on 17 Nov 2026); the dossier says PushOwl and 2,030 reviews, so name and count are out of date. The Install button was clicked and Install was approved on the permission screen (View customer data, View staff and contributor data, View and edit store data) at about 22:53. The app opens in its own PushOwl dashboard (dashboard.pushowl.io), logged in automatically through Shopify; no separate Brevo account or password was asked. Onboarding asks where to start (Web Push, Email, SMS) and then shows an Ad Studio screen with Continue to free trial, which was not clicked. The Home page shows First steps 0 / 4 (Activate the app embed, subscribers, Verify your email, Verify your mobile number); the phone verification was not done. Core action: about 7 minutes and about 8 steps after the install, at about 23:00, the first result was on screen. Automations shows Welcome notifications as Active, switched on by default on Basic. The preview shows the trigger When a new visitor subscribes, Reminder 1 after 0 minutes (You are subscribed / We will keep you posted with latest updates), Reminder 2 after 2 hours (We're glad to have you here!) and Reminder 3 after 1 day (Hey there! Anything specific caught your eye?); Reminder 2 and 3 are Inactive. Forms, Create campaign, Popup offers templates (Rival, Frond, Fizz, Lumina, Scoop, Villa, Studio, Edit); Rival Spin to win was chosen and its preview was seen at the step Theme. Nothing was saved or published and the wizard was left with Leave (Your customizations haven't been saved yet). Native Browser Prompt is Active and iOS Install Prompt is Inactive; browser push permission was not accepted (the Let's go! modal was closed). Nothing was sent. Locked automations on Basic: Abandoned cart recovery says it is available on the Plus bundle (with a free trial button), Browse abandonment is available on the Power bundle and Shipping notifications are locked too. Back in stock and Price drop can be switched on; they were not switched on. Plans: the Pricing page shows Basic bundle, Current plan, $0.00, Web push impressions 0 / 500 and Email credits 0 / 500 (equal to the dossier), Plus bundle $19.00 (10.000 push, 1.000 email credits) and Power bundle $79.00 (25.000 push, 1.500 email credits); SMS has 0 credits on every plan and credits are bought separately. The listing shows Plus at $19 / month ($180/year), which is $15 a month, equal to the dossier ($19 a month, $15 billed yearly). The buttons Start 14-day free trial and the Trial plans tab were not used. Checkout: Select plan on Plus opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: Plus bundle, $19,00 USD every 30 days, subtotal $19,00 plus any applicable taxes, total due 17 Nov $19,00, an Add payment method row and a greyed out Approve button. The sentence that you will not be billed for this test charge was NOT on the screen, so Plus was not approved, no card was added and Cancel was clicked. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so there was nothing to cancel. Settings, Apps, the app menu and Uninstall opens the dialog Uninstall Brevo PushOwl? which says you will no longer be able to use the app and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required before Uninstall becomes active (Testing multiple apps was chosen). Not tested: sending a real push or e-mail, browser push permission, verifying a mobile number or an e-mail address, Activate (the app embed in the theme), Ad Studio, the trial and the paid plans, SMS and switching on Back in stock or Price drop. Clean up: at about 23:12 the app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps and no longer showed under Installed. No popup was saved, no campaign was made, no e-mail or push was sent and the plan stayed Basic. Our own tab was closed. The price fields are not changed here. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The dossier is out of date on the name (the listing is now Brevo PushOwl: Email,Push,SMS) and on the review count (2,321 today against 2,030). Abandoned cart recovery, the automation most shops want, needs the Plus bundle, and the Plus approval screen asks for a payment method without a test charge sentence. The app starts on a free plan with a welcome flow already on, but it sends nothing until the app embed is activated and visitors subscribe, which was not tried.

Export and reimport.
